body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{crit}}\), derive the complete \(s=1\) cutoff/effect-label limit experiments separately on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{slope}}\), where \(\tau_n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)\), and on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},0}\cup\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},\lambda}\), where \(\tau_n\to\infty\) and \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)\). Include boundary-truncated mixtures and every surviving second-order coordinate. Evaluate the fixed-\(\alpha\) minimax expected connected-interval length as \(\mathcal V_\alpha(\tau,\lambda;1)\), and determine whether causal-valid location mixtures together with same-class slope-kink alternatives are least favorable in the full model. Require only the certified reduction \(\mathcal V_\alpha(0,0;1)=2(1-\alpha)\) at the flat boundary; no exact value is asserted on a finite-positive face before the decision problem is solved.
body.justification: The non-Gaussian decision value, rather than cutoff consistency alone, is the unresolved critical object governing honest interval length.
body.gap: Elliott and M\"uller (2014) solve a parametric moderate-break process problem and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022) give an abstract weak-GMM decision theory; Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) keep the fuzzy-RD cutoff fixed. None derives this binary H\"older moving-cutoff experiment, its signed causal label, or its connected-length value.
body.consumer: The value map tells fuzzy-RD users how much interval informativeness remains at each empirically relevant combination of weak compliance and cutoff uncertainty.
